false_urgency.name: False urgency
false_urgency.description: Falsely stating or implying urgency or scarcity to rush a purchase.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

false_urgency.fix: Show a real end time that does not move, or remove the countdown. Show stock levels only when they come from live inventory.

basket_sneaking.name: Basket sneaking
basket_sneaking.description: Adding products, services or charges to the cart without the user’s consent.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

basket_sneaking.fix: Never add items to the cart for the shopper. Offer add-ons as an unticked option with the price shown next to it.

confirm_shaming.name: Confirm shaming
confirm_shaming.description: Using guilt, fear or ridicule to steer the user towards a choice.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

confirm_shaming.fix: Use neutral decline wording such as “No thanks”, and give the popup a visible close button.

forced_action.name: Forced action
forced_action.description: Forcing an unrelated action (sign-up, app download, purchase) to continue.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

forced_action.fix: Let shoppers finish the purchase without signing up, downloading an app or buying something unrelated.

subscription_trap.name: Subscription trap
subscription_trap.description: Enrolling users in recurring payments by default or making exit hard.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

subscription_trap.fix: Leave memberships unticked by default, show the recurring price in normal type, and allow one-click online cancellation.

interface_interference.name: Interface interference
interface_interference.description: Visual design that highlights one option and obscures the alternative.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

interface_interference.fix: Give paid and free choices equal visual weight, for example two equally styled options.

bait_and_switch.name: Bait and switch
bait_and_switch.description: Advertising one outcome and delivering another, usually costlier.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

bait_and_switch.fix: Only advertise variants and prices that are actually available to buy.

drip_pricing.name: Drip pricing
drip_pricing.description: Revealing charges only late in the journey instead of upfront.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

drip_pricing.fix: Include every unavoidable fee in the price shown on the product page, or show it clearly beside that price.

disguised_advertisement.name: Disguised advertisement
disguised_advertisement.description: Paid placements presented as editorial or organic content.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

disguised_advertisement.fix: Label paid placements clearly as ads or sponsored content.

nagging.name: Nagging
nagging.description: Repeated requests or interruptions unrelated to the purchase.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

nagging.fix: Ask once, respect the answer, and do not repeat the prompt during the same visit.

trick_question.name: Trick question
trick_question.description: Confusing or double-negative wording that misleads the user’s choice.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

trick_question.fix: Write consent choices as plain, positive statements, without double negatives.

saas_billing.name: SaaS billing
saas_billing.description: Recurring charges collected silently, e.g. after a free trial.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

saas_billing.fix: Remind users before a trial converts to paid, and charge only with clear consent.

rogue_malware.name: Rogue malware
rogue_malware.description: Software that misleads users into paying or installing malware.

rule.source: CCPA Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023

rogue_malware.fix: Remove any software that misleads users into paying or installing it.

misleading_price.name: Inflated reference price
misleading_price.description: A discount calculated off an MRP that was never the real selling price.

rule.clause: Sec. 2(28) misleading advertisement; Sec. 2(47) unfair trade practice

misleading_price.fix: Compare against a price the product was genuinely sold at recently (for example the lowest price of the last 30 days), not an inflated MRP.
